t: Ancient and modern figures for Roman dead range from 10,500 to 16,000 (Cantalupi) to 70,000 (Polybius), and figures for ancient battles, Carthaginian ones above all, are often unreliable.
Hannibal's centre gave ground step by step while his African infantry and cavalry closed round the Romans, who were packed so tightly that they could hardly use their weapons.
Rome did not accept Hannibal's offer to ransom prisoners or to make peace, raised new legions and fought on for 14 more years until the Battle of Zama.
dyk: Within three campaign seasons, about 20 months, Rome is said to have lost one fifth, some 150,000, of its male citizens over 17, and it buried people alive as a sacrifice after the defeat.
ev: Hannibal crosses the Pyrenees and Alps into Italy and defeats the Romans at the Trebia
Hannibal defeats the Romans at Lake Trasimene, and Quintus Fabius Maximus is made dictator and avoids pitched battle
Varro and Paullus are elected consuls and given a newly raised army of unprecedented size
Hannibal seizes the supply depot at Cannae and the consuls march south to meet him
Hannibal's army encircles and destroys most of the Roman army at Cannae
Capua and other Italian cities defect to Hannibal; Rome rejects his offer to ransom prisoners
Hannibal first attacks Rome, five years after Cannae

f.date: 2 August 216 BCE according to Macrobius, citing the annalist Quadrigarius; P. S. Derow identified the Julian equivalent as 1 July 216 BCE, and others have suggested other dates
f.place: Near the ancient village of Cannae on the left bank of the river Aufidus in Apulia, south-east Italy
f.sides: Rome and its Italian allies under the consuls Lucius Aemilius Paullus and Gaius Terentius Varro, with approximately 86,000 men by a general estimate; Carthage and its allies under Hannibal, perhaps 40,000 to 50,000, a figure to be treated with caution
f.outcome: Most of the Roman army was surrounded and killed; ancient and modern figures for the dead range widely. Capua and several other Italian cities went over to Hannibal, but Rome refused to make peace.
